newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Bodies of two executed men found in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Bodies of two executed men found in Cambodia.

text.p: Human rights investigators in Cambodia on Thursday found the decaying bodies of two executed men they feared had been loyalists of ousted premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Rights workers and diplomatic sources say at least 40 supporters of First Prime Minister Ranariddh have been killed in the aftermath of his bloody overthrow by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on July 6.
The two bodies found on Thursday were buried in shallow graves in a gully off a main road 100 km (60 miles) southwest of Phnom Penh. They had been bound, blindfolded and shot.
"Both appear to have been shot in the head and blindfolded and handcuffed," said Brad Adams of the U.N. Centre for Human Rights in Cambodia.
"We don't know who they are, we do know that they were clearly executed," he said. "They were taken there and shot and then buried."
"We're concerned they may be FUNCINPEC soldiers or other people reported missing in the last weeks," Adams said referring to Ranariddh's royalist political party.
Villagers in the area said they had seen military trucks driving to the gully beside the road to the port city of Sihanoukville, a member of the U.N. rights team said.
"We think there are more bodies around the country," said the team member who declined to be identified.
Hun Sen's government has said one senior royalist official was executed after his arrest. Several other senior FUNCINPEC officials are known to hve been killed.

Hun Sen has denied human rights abuses and invited rights groups to investigate the situation in the country. He also said members of parliament from all parties would look in to reports of rights abuses.
Some 60 people were killed and almost 200 wounded in two days of battles on the streets of the capital earlier this month as forces under the rival prime ministers clashed.
Hundreds of Ranariddh's soldiers and supporters were detained after his ouster and rights United Nations' officials said earlier some of them were tortured.

Many members of Ranariddh's party and royalists fled from Cambodia after Hun Sen's coup and others went in to hiding. Ranariddh told reporters in Singapore earlier this week that Hun Sen forces had killed at least 600 of his supporters.
